intro: Harmony-heavy Americana with a Grateful Dead streak.
story: Cordovas is led by the songwriter Joe Firstman, a former Atlantic Records solo artist and house-band leader on Last Call with Carson Daly, and formed in 2011 with a self-titled debut in 2012. That Santa Fe Channel, their ATO debut, came out on August 10, 2018, and The Line of Best Fit gave it 9/10. They played Pickathon in 2019. The Rose of Aces, their fifth album, followed in 2023, and Americana UK named it to its Top 20 of the year; in 2026 they began a weekly residency in Todos Santos, Baja California.

intro: A Montreal songwriter whose songs sound close and hushed.
story: Helena Deland was born in Vancouver, raised in Quebec City and is based in Montreal; her Drawing Room EP came out on Chivi Chivi in 2016. In 2018 she released the Altogether Unaccompanied series on Luminelle Recordings, started by Gorilla vs. Bear's Chris Cantalini, Vol. I and II in March and Vol. III and IV on October 19. She played Pickathon in 2019. Someone New, her first full-length, came out on Luminelle in 2020 and made the Polaris Prize longlist in 2021, and Goodnight Summerland followed in 2023.

intro: Andrew Marlin and Emily Frantz's close, unhurried harmonies.
story: Tides of a Teardrop came out on Yep Roc on February 1, 2019, their fifth album, reaching No. 164 on the Billboard 200 and No. 2 on the Folk chart; Marlin has said the album is about the death of his mother. They came to Pickathon that year, their fourth visit. In 2021 they renamed the duo Watchhouse, and the self-titled Watchhouse came out on Thirty Tigers on August 13. Rituals followed in 2025.

Marian Azeb Mereba was born on September 19, 1990, with Ethiopian roots, and is an Atlanta-based singer, rapper and producer who signed to Interscope in 2018. Her major-label debut, The Jungle Is the Only Way Out, came out on February 27, 2019, with 6LACK and JID as guests, and she played Pickathon that year. She appeared on Spillage Village's Spilligion in September 2020, and The Breeze Grew a Fire followed on Secretly Canadian.

intro: New Orleans traditional jazz, played in the hall's own style.
story: Allan Jaffe, a tuba player, formed the Preservation Hall Jazz Band in the early 1960s; his son Ben Jaffe, who plays bass and tuba and runs the Hall as creative director, took over after Allan died in 1987. The band traveled to Cuba in December 2015, which became the film and album A Tuba to Cuba; the documentary premiered at Sundance in January 2019 and the soundtrack came out on Sub Pop on June 28. Jaffe described it as like listening to the radio, a conversation across strange FM wavelengths. They played Pickathon in 2019. For Fat Man, with Preservation Brass, came out in 2025 and was nominated for the Grammy for Best Regional Roots Music Album.

Sam Owens of Brooklyn, formerly of the band Celestial Shore, helped build the Figure 8 recording studios and worked there as an engineer before going solo as Sam Evian in 2016. Premium came out on Saddle Creek that year, You, Forever in 2018 and Time to Melt in 2021. He played Pickathon in 2019. He produced Big Thief's Dragon New Warm Mountain I Believe in You in 2022, and Plunge came out on March 22, 2024, recorded live to tape at his Catskills studio, the first on his own Flying Cloud Recordings imprint with Thirty Tigers.

intro: An Auckland quartet of big, bright guitar hooks.
story: The Beths formed in 2014 at the University of Auckland: Elizabeth Stokes, Jonathan Pearce, Benjamin Sinclair and Tristan Deck. Future Me Hates Me came out on Carpark on August 10, 2018, produced by Pearce at his K' Road studio, and Rolling Stone called it a power-pop monument. Stokes said she liked naming the band after herself, the way Lorelai Gilmore named her daughter after herself. They played Pickathon in 2019. Jump Rope Gazers followed in 2020, Expert in a Dying Field in 2022 and Straight Line Was a Lie on Anti- in 2025.

intro: A Los Angeles art-rock band led by John Rossiter.
story: Young Jesus is a Chicago band that began in the suburbs and has been based in Los Angeles since 2014; it signed to Saddle Creek in 2017. The Whole Thing Is Just There came out on October 12, 2018, six songs over 50 minutes, and John Rossiter said the title comes from a Philip Guston video about the feeling that the whole thing is just there. Stereogum named them a Band to Watch. They played Pickathon in 2019. Welcome to Conceptual Beach followed in 2020, Shepherd Head in 2022 and The Fool in 2024, all on Saddle Creek.
